subject: SCIENCE
title: Classify the Animals
objective: Classify animals by observable traits and explain the chosen rule.
introduction: Milo has cards showing feathers, swimming, and scales. How can Maxine group animals using traits she can observe?

vocabulary.definition: To sort things into groups that are alike.
A feature you can notice on a living thing, such as feathers or scales.
A feature or quality a living thing has.

activities.instruction: Watch Milo group animals using traits he can observe.
activities.content: A learner-made group is an observation tool, not formal biological taxonomy.

feedback.retry: Check that the trait can be seen, then use the same rule for every card.

activities.accessibilityAlternative: Text alternative: A learner-made group is an observation tool, not formal biological taxonomy.

activities.instruction: Tap each card and notice the animal trait shown.

feedback.correct: Great! You found the examples for Classify the Animals. 🔎
feedback.retry: Name the visible trait on each animal before grouping it.

activities.accessibilityAlternative: A numbered list of the same examples is available for keyboard and screen-reader use.

activities.instruction: Sort each observation by whether it is a visible animal trait.

feedback.correct: Great sorting! Your groups are correct.
feedback.retry: Ask whether each card describes something you can observe on an animal.

activities.accessibilityAlternative: Tap an item and then tap a labeled category; dragging is optional.

activities.instruction: Choose the rule that uses a trait you can observe.

feedback.correct: Correct: has feathers or no feathers
feedback.retry: Choose a trait that eyes can notice, not a feeling or guess.

activities.accessibilityAlternative: All choices are visible text and selectable with TalkBack.

activities.instruction: Match each observation with the kind of grouping rule it supports.

feedback.correct: Great! You matched each example with its Classify the Animals explanation. 🔗
feedback.retry: Match each observation with the kind of rule it can support.

activities.accessibilityAlternative: A list-based matching control replaces drag gestures.

activities.instruction: Order the steps for grouping animals by an observable trait.

feedback.correct: Great! You put the Classify the Animals steps in order. 🎉
feedback.retry: Check the order: choose a visible trait, sort the cards, then state the rule.

activities.accessibilityAlternative: Up and down buttons provide an alternative to dragging.

items.prompt: Milo groups animal cards by feathers, scales, or movement. Which statement is true?

options.text: Sorting by what you can observe is a useful grouping rule.
Group animals by Maxine's favorite color
Use a trait no one can observe

items.explanation: A visible trait gives you evidence for a group, but it does not create an official species name. Favorite color and invisible guesses are not traits of the animal.

items.prompt: Maxine sees a robin and a fish on two cards. Which grouping rule uses a trait she can see?
items.explanation: Feathers are visible on a robin, so they are an observable trait. Niceness, luck, and favorite color do not describe a body feature.

items.prompt: Milo wants groups based on the animals, not his own likes. Which rule should he NOT use?

options.text: Group by feathers or no feathers
Group by scales or no scales

items.explanation: Favorite color describes Milo's preference, not an animal trait. Feathers, movement, and scales can be observed on the animals.

items.prompt: A learner looks at a lizard card. Which rule uses an observable trait?
items.explanation: Scales are visible on a lizard, so they can be used as an observable grouping trait. Feelings and luck cannot be seen as body features.

items.prompt: Maxine sorts cards after looking at each animal. Which rule groups animals by something she can see?

options.text: Group by how much Maxine likes them

items.explanation: Scales can be seen, so they provide evidence for a grouping rule. Likes, favorite colors, and invisible traits do not describe the animal.
